The compound is identified as a target of Disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein 28, which in turn is targeted by (2S)-3',4'-Dihydroxy-6,7-Dimethoxyflavan. This chain of targets implies a possible regulatory pathway where the initial compound may influence the activity of the second, which ultimately affects Thrombopoietin. The evidence supports a mechanistic link, though the exact nature of the interactions remains unclear. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it relies on indirect associations through target proteins, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct relationship between the compound and Thrombopoietin.
